title: Sector Nine Rising Anew
premise: Edmund Coldharbour, a clone carrying the original's unsolved murder case in her memory, works the long-haul freight route between worlds that severed contact after the Silence. When a manifest for the Meridian—a ship that never flew—lists her original's name alongside a stranger's, she realizes someone is broadcasting fragments of her past toward the dead relay at Sector Nine. Pursued by the Consortium agents who want the case buried and shadowed by Vess, a stowaway engineer who knew the original, Edmund races to reach the relay first. At the relay she discovers the signal is a message from the original herself, recorded before her death: proof that the Consortium ordered the murder of every clone who remembered too much. Edmund must choose between destroying the evidence to protect her found crew or transmitting it and ending her own anonymity forever; she transmits, and the rising signal finally makes the silent worlds listen.
about_author: J. M. Nakamura is a former merchant marine radio operator who spent eleven years on deep-space supply runs before turning to fiction. Their novels are known for claustrophobic shipboard atmospheres and characters who carry other people's ghosts.

chapters.title: The Long Quiet
chapters.summary: Edmund Coldharbour pilots freighter Kestrel's Wake along the silent trade lanes, establishing her solitary routine and the murder memories she keeps locked away. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: weary contentment built on deliberate forgetting.

chapters.title: Manifest Anomaly
chapters.summary: At Port Calloway, dockmaster Ilo hands Edmund a corrupted manifest for the Meridian, a hull decommissioned before it ever launched. Her original's name appears beside an unknown: R. Vess. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: cold dread cracking open old grief.

chapters.title: Questions at the Dock
chapters.summary: Edmund investigates the Meridian's records and finds the file scrubbed within hours of her asking. A Consortium liaison, Agent Serevan, takes polite interest in her questions. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Stowaway
chapters.summary: Mid-jump, Edmund finds Vess hiding in the cargo bay—an engineer who claims she served with the original Coldharbour and recognized the name on the manifest. POV: alternating Edmund and Vess. Emotional beat: hostile suspicion meeting desperate honesty.

chapters.title: What Vess Remembers
chapters.summary: Vess recounts the original Edmund's final voyage: secret cargo, a relay visit, and a warning that 'they erase what remembers.' Edmund tests the story against her inherited memories. POV: Vess. Emotional beat: reluctant kinship between two people haunted by one woman.

chapters.title: Signal in the Static
chapters.summary: Kestrel's Wake picks up a repeating burst from dead space—fragments of the original's voice. Someone is feeding the relay. Serevan hails the ship, requesting boarding. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: the past becoming audible, unavoidable.

chapters.title: Boarding Party
chapters.summary: Serevan's inspection finds nothing, but he leaves a tracker Edmund only barely detects. She and Vess realize the Consortium wants them led somewhere—or followed there. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: hunted calm, trust tentatively forming.

chapters.title: Hollow Station
chapters.summary: They divert to abandoned refueling station Threnody, where a dying caretaker AI confirms the Meridian was real, crewed by clones, and erased from record after its single flight. POV: Vess. Emotional beat: horror at the scale of the erasure.

chapters.title: Crew of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Station records reveal the Meridian carried seven clones of Edmund's original—all now unaccounted for. Vess admits she was hired to find them before they were found first. POV: Vess. Emotional beat: betrayal, then forgiveness as motives align.

chapters.title: Consortium Shadow
chapters.summary: A hunter vessel shadows them through the dark lanes. Edmund executes a brutal slingshot maneuver through debris fields to break pursuit, damaging the Kestrel's Wake. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: fierce competence masking fear.

chapters.title: Repairs and Confessions
chapters.summary: Stranded for repairs, Edmund and Vess share their histories—the clone's stolen life, the deserter's guilt. They become something like family, joined by mechanic druid-unit PATCH, the ship's ancient AI. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: found family crystallizing under pressure.

chapters.title: The Second Voice
chapters.summary: The signal strengthens: two voices now, the original and another clone, arguing about whether to transmit. The second voice goes silent mid-sentence. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: grief arriving ahead of understanding.

chapters.title: Serevan's Offer
chapters.summary: Serevan catches up and offers Edmund immunity and a new identity if she surrenders Vess and lets the relay die. He reveals the original was killed for what she carried. POV: Serevan. Emotional beat: temptation framed as mercy.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Edmund refuses, and Serevan's hunters cripple the Kestrel's Wake's drives. Vess performs a dangerous EVA repair while Edmund draws fire. POV: Vess. Emotional beat: loyalty proven in vacuum and fire.

chapters.title: Into Dead Space
chapters.summary: Running on patched engines, they cross the boundary into Sector Nine's dead zone where no rescue exists and the relay's beacon burns cold ahead. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: point of no return, terror and freedom together.

chapters.title: The Relay
chapters.summary: Docking with the ancient relay, they find evidence of the other clones—one grave, one empty bunk still warm. The transmitter holds a queued message addressed to 'whoever inherits me.' POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: standing inside the original's last days.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: The recording plays: the original documented the Consortium's clone-erasure program and named her killer—Serevan himself. She left the choice of transmission to her inheritor, knowing either path costs everything. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: devastating clarity of purpose.

chapters.title: Hunter's Arrival
chapters.summary: Serevan boards the relay with armed teams. In the station's corridors, Edmund confronts him with the truth of his crime while Vess fights to keep the transmitter powered. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: climax—truth versus survival made literal.

chapters.title: Transmit
chapters.summary: Wounded, Edmund triggers the broadcast. The evidence floods every listening channel in the sector as Serevan's forces close in—and then falter, orders countermanding orders as the truth spreads faster than it can be suppressed. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: sacrifice transformed into victory.

chapters.title: Aftermath at the Edge
chapters.summary: With Serevan arrested by his own command structure, Edmund and Vess limp home as the silent worlds begin answering each other again, traffic resuming lane by lane. POV: Vess. Emotional beat: exhausted wonder at a universe reopening.

chapters.title: Names on the Manifest
chapters.summary: At Port Calloway, the Meridian's crew is formally restored to the record, all seven names read aloud. Edmund signs as witness, claiming her inheritance openly for the first time. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: grief honored, identity chosen rather than assigned.

chapters.title: Rising Anew
chapters.summary: Edmund accepts a commission to run the reopened routes as an independent courier, Vess and PATCH aboard. The long road ahead is no longer escape but purpose. Final image: the Kestrel's Wake jumping toward a world that speaks. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: hopeful departure, family intact.
